purpose: Map executable-solution requirements to their current governed owner before proposing architecture changes.

classificationSemantics.PRESENT_SUFFICIENT_FOR_CURRENT_ROLE: The current layer explicitly owns the requirement at the appropriate abstraction level.
classificationSemantics.PRESENT_PARTIAL: Some semantics exist but are not sufficient for the challenged solution-design use case.
classificationSemantics.PRESENT_AFTER_RUNTIME_SELECTED: The requirement is handled only after a target runtime/adapter has already been chosen.
classificationSemantics.CLIENT_BINDING: The requirement is legitimately client/environment-specific and should not be promoted into global canonical truth.
classificationSemantics.ABSENT_AS_GOVERNED_SELECTION_SEMANTIC: No first-class governed mechanism was found for using this requirement in cross-runtime solution generation/selection.
classificationSemantics.PENDING_CONTRACT: Conceptual ownership exists but the machine-readable canonical contract is not implemented.

requirements.requirement: semantic work purpose and business outcome
business rules, controls and decision logic
inputs, outputs, information and canonical objects
requirements.note: R0.3 proves current Road LTL object and information contracts remain materially incomplete; architecture ownership exists even though knowledge coverage does not.

requirements.requirement: exceptions, escalation, retry, recovery
human authority and human boundary
executor classes and executor-specific stopping criteria
client application, system and environment
client fields/API mappings
master/network/configuration data
client SLA, cut-off and policy thresholds
client organization, approval authority and escalation routing
security, credential and environment binding
interface mechanism API/EDI/event/file/document/UI/message
runtime capability and constraint declaration
runtime compatibility/loss assessment for a WorkDefinition
runtime projection generation and verification
SLA/deadline/schedule semantics
cost/revenue/quality/service/risk measurement
requirements.note: Measurement exists, but no governed selection function was found that uses measures to compare solution candidates.

requirements.requirement: workload volume, arrival pattern, peak/seasonality and concurrency demand
latency/throughput requirement used for architecture selection
requirements.note: Time constraints exist; no explicit design-selection consumption contract found.

requirements.requirement: ambiguity/variability level used to choose deterministic vs probabilistic execution
confidence/risk tolerance and HITL threshold used for solution selection
human capacity, skill, coverage and staffing constraints
availability, resilience, RTO/RPO and observability requirements
transaction/idempotency/atomicity/compensation semantics
parallel branches, joins, correlation and multi-instance semantics
durable state ownership/persistence and timeout ownership
generate multiple feasible execution architectures
compose hybrid solution across multiple executor/runtime types
requirements.note: Hybrid executability is recognized, but no governed composition/synthesis mechanism was found.

requirements.requirement: compare candidate architectures across fit, cost, risk, SLA and constraints
record selection rationale and rejected alternatives
select target runtime adapter(s)
requirements.note: The documented flow contains the action to select a target runtime adapter but does not define the governed reasoning/contract that performs the selection.

requirements.requirement: trace canonical rule through client binding, design decision and runtime projection
requirements.note: Traceability exists across adjacent layers, but a missing design-decision artifact would leave the solution-choice step ungoverned.

summary.primaryConfirmedStrength: Atlas already separates canonical work, client-specific binding and runtime projection with strong executor-neutrality.
summary.primaryChallenge: Cross-runtime solution synthesis, comparison and selection are not currently first-class governed semantics.
summary.secondaryChallenge: Pending Work Decomposition / WorkDefinition contracts require explicit grammar review before implementation.
